1 · Your Chapter

Do this first. Pick your Chapter from the list and your logo, your Chapter name and your Chapter and Region numbers all fill in for you. Posting for the whole region? Pick Southeast. Posting for the global page? Pick The AI Collective and the cards name no city at all.

Your name and contact end every post text. We recommend you be the contact. When a sponsor reaches you first, the lead is yours and you earn the 5% referral. If you would rather not, leave both blank and the post sends leads to Mark Michelson, Region Director, at mark@aicollective.com or Calendly.com/michelson. The tool remembers what you type on this device.

Got a sponsor lead? Send it in with the referral form. The regional office closes it and you earn 5%. Or close it yourself in Sponsor Studio and earn the full 15%. 15% is the most anyone earns on a deal.

A big Chapter should lead with its own number. A new one should lead with the network it belongs to. On Pick the strongest one for me the tool climbs the ladder for you: your Chapter if it has at least 250 members, then your Region, then worldwide. You never have to post a number that makes you look small.

2 · Logo and picture

Southeast Chapters: pick your Chapter in step 1 and both logos load for you. Upload your own only if your Chapter is not in the list.

On the headshot card the standard AIC classroom photo fills the bottom until you add your own.

Use one. A room full of faces is the whole argument. If your Chapter has not run an event yet, take the standard photo. It is a real AIC room, and a real room beats an empty frame or a stock illustration. Swap it for your own the week after your first event.

Built from Where the link goes in section 6, with your Chapter tag added so the traffic it brings shows up as yours. Change the address there.

Top right, level with your logo, and on headshot cards it moves down beside the cue. Worth it on the partner card, on anything you print, and on a slide at an event. Useless in a phone feed, because nobody can scan their own screen. The QR is the one thing on the card a phone can actually act on, so it earns its place off a screen and nowhere else.

4 · Partner card

It goes to the right of your Chapter logo and is the biggest thing on the card. On a colored background it sits on a white plate so any logo reads.

Not drawn on the card. It goes into the post copy under the preview. Tag them with @ when you post.

Sponsors do not care whether the banner holds 13 logos or 300. They care that one of them is theirs, that it is seen all year, and that it says they back people applying AI intelligently in their own community. Lead with what they get.

"What you get" is the only one of the three a sponsor cares about. The other two are for your own pipeline and for a proposal you send to a named prospect.

4 · Your headshot card

Three things put you on the card. Fill in all three so people know who you are. Use a nickname if you like. Have fun with it, as long as it is really you.

1. Upload your photo
2. Your name and title
3. Your company or organization

These three lines sit under your photo. A line you leave blank does not show.

Your message

Keep both lines together to 12 words or fewer. People read the black line and maybe the orange one. That is all. {city} becomes your Chapter name.

Have them contact you first. When a sponsor reaches out to you, the lead is yours. You earn 5% when that sponsor pays, and up to 15% if you close the deal yourself. Always paste the post text under the card so people know how to reach you.

4 · Holiday card

A seasonal thank-you that keeps your Chapter in front of people. Three to pick from: Thanksgiving, Happy Holidays, and Happy New Year. Each one shows up a few weeks ahead and goes away after its day passes.

Print this one this week. Download the IG portrait size. It fits a standard 8.5 x 11 sheet. Put a copy on the check-in table at your Thanksgiving-week events, and post it too.

The holiday picture sits top right, where a headshot goes. Each holiday picks its own background. Change it in step 3 if you like.

4 · Luma card

A simple sponsor ask to drop into any Luma event. Download the square size, add it as an image in the event description, then paste the Luma text from below the preview right under it. Whoever is running the event gets the lead.

Add the organizer's headshot above if you have one. Without it, the card shows a "Free AI education" badge. Leave the organizer blank and the card sends sponsors to Mark Michelson, Region Director.

4 · Thank your partners

Post this after every month's events. It is the thing they paid for, it costs you nothing, and it is most of your renewal conversation.

Tier sets the size. First upload defaults to Platinum, next two Gold, next four Silver, the rest Bronze. Change any of them. Never show a Bronze logo at Gold size, or you have quietly given away what Gold costs.

6 · The link cue

Nothing drawn on a picture is clickable. Post an image to LinkedIn, Facebook, or Instagram and it arrives as flat pixels, so a button shape is a promise the image cannot keep. Somebody taps it, nothing happens, and you have spent your one click. What follows is the honest version: a cue that tells them where the link actually is.

8 · Export

Your browser confirms each save, so every image needs one tap. Trim Sizes above to the one or two formats you actually post and this stays quick.

The image is not the link. The caption is. Nothing drawn on a picture is clickable on LinkedIn, Facebook, or Instagram, so the card points at the link and the caption carries the ask. Every caption ends with your contact info, so an interested sponsor reaches you. When one does, send their details in with the referral form and we will help you close it.
What an annual sponsor gets

Platinum, 1 spot. Top of the Chapter banner under the Chapter logo. Chapter landing page. Logo and link on every Luma invitation. The partner slide at every education event, and the welcome. Registration list. 20% off event sponsorships.

Gold, 2 spots. Banner below Platinum. Landing page. Logo and link on Luma. Slides and welcome. Registration list. 20% off events.

Silver, 4 spots. Banner below Gold. Landing page. Link on Luma. Logo on Luma, slides, and registration list when they also sponsor that event. 10% off events.

Bronze, 6 spots. Banner and a verbal call-out at events. Link on Luma. 5% off events.

Annual terms run 12 months. Banners print up to twice a year, so a late sponsor waits for the next print. That is the honest reason to sign now.

How to run this

Weeks 1 to 3. Why the work matters. Control, clear thinking, in person, free.

Weeks 4 to 6. The banner and the 13 spots. Start direct outreach to named people at banks, credit unions, universities, law firms, and the chamber.

Weeks 7 and 8. Count down what is left.

Headshot cards run the whole time. A named organizer with a face beats a Chapter logo every time.

Caption carries the detail. The image says one thing. The caption is where the events, the numbers, and the tiers go. Keep them off the picture.

Now copy the post text. Never post the card alone.

The card gets attention. The words under it make the case. These four options are written to back up the sentence on your card, and they change when you change the sentence. Pick one, tap Copy, and paste it as your post text with the image. Each ends with your name and contact, so the lead comes to you. Written for LinkedIn and short enough for Facebook. On Instagram, put your contact in your bio too.
